records.source: Καὶ πάλιν ἤρξατο διδάσκειν παρὰ τὴν θάλασσαν.
records.gloss: And again he began to teach beside the sea.
pieces: Once more {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} began teaching by the lake.

L.1: And again {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} began to teach beside the sea.

R.1: Another time Jesus began to teach beside Lake Galilee.

decisions.choice: the sea: the Sea of Galilee, a freshwater lake
decisions.reason: Mark calls the lake of Galilee "the sea", as in 1:16 and 3:7.

decisions.choice: again: Jesus teaches by the lake once more
decisions.reason: He had taught crowds by the lake before (2:13; 3:7-9).

decisions.choice: the lake (B); Lake Galilee (R)
decisions.reason: As in chapters 1-3, Balanced and Readable call it a lake, which is what it is.

records.heading: A farmer goes out to sow

records.source: καὶ συνάγεται πρὸς αὐτὸν ὄχλος πλεῖστος, ὥστε αὐτὸν εἰς πλοῖον ἐμβάντα καθῆσθαι ἐν τῇ θαλάσσῃ, καὶ πᾶς ὁ ὄχλος πρὸς τὴν θάλασσαν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ἦσαν.
records.gloss: And is gathered together to him a crowd very great, so that he into a boat having embarked sat in the sea, and all the crowd toward the sea on the land were.
pieces: The crowd that gathered around {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} was so enormous that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} stepped into a boat and sat in it out on the water, while all the people stayed on the shore by the lake.

L.1: And a very great crowd gathers to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, so that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} got into a boat and sat [in it] on the sea, and the whole crowd was beside the sea on the land.

R.1: A very large crowd came together around {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. So Jesus stepped into a boat. He sat down in it, out on the water. All the people stood on the shore by the lake.

decisions.choice: gathers: a present tense telling a past event
alternatives: the crowd is still gathering now
decisions.reason: Mark often tells past events in the present tense to make the story vivid. The sense is past.

decisions.choice: very great: the largest crowd yet
alternatives: the greatest crowd of all time
decisions.reason: The form is a superlative used to mean "very large".

decisions.choice: sat: teachers sat to teach
decisions.reason: A Jewish teacher sat while his hearers listened (Matthew 5:1; Luke 4:20). The boat kept the crowd from pressing on him, as 3:9 planned.

decisions.choice: gathered (B); came together (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable tell the story in the past tense.

records.source: καὶ ἐδίδασκεν αὐτοὺς ἐν παραβολαῖς πολλά καὶ ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς ἐν τῇ διδαχῇ αὐτοῦ·
records.gloss: And he was teaching them in parables many things, and was saying to them in the teaching of him,
pieces: He used parables to teach them many things, and as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} taught {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them,

L.2: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was teaching them many things in parables, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was saying to them in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} teaching,

R.2: He taught them many things by telling stories. As {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} taught, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them,

decisions.choice: parables: stories or sayings that compare one thing with another
decisions.reason: A parable sets a picture from daily life beside a truth about God's kingdom. The word can also mean a riddle or dark saying, which matters in 4:11.

decisions.choice: was teaching, was saying: the teaching went on for some time
decisions.reason: The verbs describe ongoing action. Mark gives a sample of what Jesus said.

decisions.choice: stories
decisions.reason: Readable calls the parables stories, as it does from 3:23.

records.source: Ἀκούετε.
records.gloss: Listen!
pieces: "Listen!

decisions.choice: listen: a call to hear with full attention
decisions.reason: The same verb opens Israel's creed, "Hear, O Israel" (Deuteronomy 6:4). Hearing is the theme of the whole parable (4:9, 23-24).

decisions.choice: to me
decisions.reason: Readable makes the call to the hearers plain.

records.source: ἰδοὺ ἐξῆλθεν ὁ σπείρων σπεῖραι.
records.gloss: Behold, went out the [one] sowing to sow.
pieces: A farmer went out to sow seed.

L.3: Look, the sower went out to sow.

R.3: A farmer went out to plant some seed.

decisions.choice: behold: look, pay attention
decisions.reason: The word draws attention to what follows.

decisions.choice: the sower: a farmer scattering seed by hand
decisions.reason: Seed was thrown by the handful from a bag as the farmer walked over the field, so some fell where it could not grow.

decisions.choice: a farmer
decisions.reason: "Sower" is an old word. Balanced and Readable name him as a farmer; the article marks a typical case, not a known man.

decisions.choice: not translated (B, R)
decisions.reason: In Balanced and Readable the story's opening words already call for attention.

records.source: καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ σπείρειν ὃ μὲν ἔπεσεν παρὰ τὴν ὁδόν, καὶ ἦλθεν τὰ πετεινὰ καὶ κατέφαγεν αὐτό.
records.gloss: And it came about in the sowing, some fell along the road, and came the birds and devoured it.
pieces: As he scattered it, some seed fell beside the path, and birds came and ate it up.

L.4: And it happened as he sowed [that] some fell along the path, and the birds came and devoured it.

R.4: As he threw the seed, some of it landed on the path. Birds came and ate it.

decisions.choice: the path: a trodden way through or beside the field
decisions.reason: Paths ran through fields and were beaten hard by feet. Seed lay on top where birds could see it.

decisions.choice: it came about: a way of starting a new event in a story
decisions.reason: The phrase follows the style of Hebrew storytelling and adds no meaning of its own.

decisions.choice: path
decisions.reason: The word is the usual one for a road, but here it is a footpath beside a field.

records.source: καὶ ἄλλο ἔπεσεν ἐπὶ τὸ πετρῶδες ὅπου οὐκ εἶχεν γῆν πολλήν, καὶ εὐθὺς ἐξανέτειλεν διὰ τὸ μὴ ἔχειν βάθος γῆς·
records.gloss: And other fell upon the rocky [ground] where not it had soil much, and immediately it sprang up because of not having depth of soil;
pieces: Some fell on rocky ground, where there was little soil. It came up quickly, since the soil was shallow.

L.5: And other [seed] fell on the rocky ground, where it did not have much soil, and immediately it sprang up because it had no depth of soil;

R.5: Some seed landed on rocky ground, where there was only a little dirt. The plants came up fast, because the dirt was not deep.

decisions.choice: rocky ground: a thin layer of soil over rock
decisions.reason: In Galilee a shallow layer of soil often lies over limestone. The farmer would not see the rock beneath.

decisions.choice: because it had no depth of soil: the shallow soil made it sprout fast
alternatives: it sprang up in spite of the shallow soil
decisions.reason: With no room to send roots down, the seed spent its strength in quick growth above ground.

decisions.choice: quickly (B); fast (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable vary the word for "immediately", as in chapters 1-3.

records.source: καὶ ὅτε ἀνέτειλεν ὁ ἥλιος ἐκαυματίσθη καὶ διὰ τὸ μὴ ἔχειν ῥίζαν ἐξηράνθη.
records.gloss: and when rose the sun it was scorched, and because of not having root it withered.
pieces: But when the sun came up, the young plants were scorched, and having no root they dried up.

L.6: and when the sun rose it was scorched, and because it had no root it withered away.

R.6: But when the sun came up, it burned the young plants. They dried up and died, because they did not have deep roots.

decisions.choice: not having root: no root that could reach water
decisions.reason: The plant had some root, but the rock stopped it from going deep (4:5).

decisions.choice: withered: dried up and died
decisions.reason: The verb means to dry out, as of a plant that dies.

decisions.choice: the young plants
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name what the seed has become.

records.source: καὶ ἄλλο ἔπεσεν εἰς τὰς ἀκάνθας, καὶ ἀνέβησαν αἱ ἄκανθαι καὶ συνέπνιξαν αὐτό, καὶ καρπὸν οὐκ ἔδωκεν.
records.gloss: And other fell into the thorns, and came up the thorns and choked it, and fruit not it gave.
pieces: Other seed fell among thorny weeds, which grew up and choked it, so that it produced no grain.

L.7: And other [seed] fell among the thorns, and the thorns came up and choked it, and it did not give fruit.

R.7: Some seed landed among thorny weeds. The weeds grew up and crowded out the young plants, so they did not produce any grain.

decisions.choice: thorns: thistles and weeds whose roots were already in the soil
decisions.reason: The ground looked clear when it was sown, but the weeds came up with the grain and were stronger.

decisions.choice: fruit: the crop, the grain
decisions.reason: For grain, "fruit" means the harvest it yields.

decisions.choice: grain
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the kind of crop.

records.source: καὶ ἄλλα ἔπεσεν εἰς τὴν γῆν τὴν καλήν, καὶ ἐδίδου καρπὸν ἀναβαίνοντα καὶ αὐξανόμενα, καὶ ἔφερεν ἓν τριάκοντα καὶ ἓν ἑξήκοντα καὶ ἓν ἑκατόν.
records.gloss: And others fell into the soil the good, and were giving fruit growing up and increasing, and were bearing one thirty and one sixty and one a hundred.
pieces: But other seed fell on good soil. It came up, grew, and produced a crop, yielding thirty, sixty, even a hundred times what was sown."

L.8: And other [seeds] fell into the good soil, and they gave fruit, growing up and increasing, and they bore thirtyfold and sixtyfold and a hundredfold."

R.8: Other seed landed on good soil. The plants came up and grew strong, and they produced a big crop. Some plants made thirty times as much grain as was planted. Some made sixty times as much, and some made a hundred times as much."

decisions.choice: one thirty, one sixty, one a hundred: each seed's yield
alternatives: in thirty, in sixty, in a hundred
decisions.reason: Early manuscripts had no accents, and the same letters can be read as "one" or "in". The SBLGNT reads "one". The sense is the same either way. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: others: plural, many seeds
decisions.reason: The earlier seed is singular; here the Greek turns to the plural, many seeds in good soil.

decisions.choice: a hundredfold: an amazing harvest
decisions.reason: Isaac reaped a hundredfold when God blessed him (Genesis 26:12). Even thirtyfold would be a very good crop.

decisions.choice: times what was sown (B); times as much grain as was planted (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the numbers measure.

records.source: καὶ ἔλεγεν· Ὃς ἔχει ὦτα ἀκούειν ἀκουέτω.
records.gloss: And he was saying, Who has ears to hear let him hear.
pieces: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "Anyone who has ears to hear should listen."

L.9: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was saying, "Whoever has ears to hear, let {{gender:them|him}} hear."

R.9: Then Jesus said, "If you have ears, then listen!"

decisions.choice: has ears to hear: is able and willing to take this in
decisions.reason: Everyone has ears; the saying calls hearers to think about what they heard and take it to heart.

decisions.choice: them (default), him (alternative)
decisions.reason: The saying is for everyone, men and women alike.

decisions.choice: If you have ears, then listen!
alternatives: whoever has ears to hear, let him hear
decisions.reason: Readable speaks to the hearer directly.

records.source: Καὶ ὅτε ἐγένετο κατὰ μόνας, ἠρώτων αὐτὸν οἱ περὶ αὐτὸν σὺν τοῖς δώδεκα τὰς παραβολάς.
records.gloss: And when he was alone, were asking him those around him with the twelve [about] the parables.
pieces: When {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was by {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}, the Twelve and the others around {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} asked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} about the parables.

L.10: And when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was alone, those around {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with the twelve were asking {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} about the parables.

R.10: Later Jesus was away from the crowd. The twelve apostles and some others who were with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} asked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} about the stories.

decisions.choice: those around him with the twelve: a wider group of followers as well as the twelve
decisions.reason: Mark names two groups. Those "around him" recall the people who sat around him in 3:34.

decisions.choice: alone: away from the crowd
decisions.reason: He is alone with his followers, not by himself.

decisions.choice: the parables: the SBLGNT has the plural
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts read the singular, or "what the parable was". Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: the Twelve (B); the twelve apostles (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced uses "the Twelve" as the group's name; Readable says who they were (3:14). Literal keeps lowercase "the twelve".

records.heading: Why Jesus speaks in parables

records.source: καὶ ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς· Ὑμῖν τὸ μυστήριον δέδοται τῆς βασιλείας τοῦ θεοῦ· ἐκείνοις δὲ τοῖς ἔξω ἐν παραβολαῖς τὰ πάντα γίνεται, ἵνα βλέποντες βλέπωσι καὶ μὴ ἴδωσιν, καὶ ἀκούοντες ἀκούωσι καὶ μὴ συνιῶσιν, μήποτε ἐπιστρέψωσιν καὶ ἀφεθῇ αὐτοῖς.
records.gloss: And he was saying to them, To you the mystery has been given of the kingdom of the God; to those but the [ones] outside in parables the all things come about, \v 12 so that seeing they may see and not perceive, and hearing they may hear and not understand, lest they turn and it be forgiven them.
pieces: He told them, "You have been given the mystery of the kingdom of God. But for those outside, everything comes in parables,
so that they may look and look but never perceive, and listen and listen but never understand; otherwise they might turn back and be forgiven."

L.11: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was saying to them, "To you the mystery of the kingdom of God has been given, but to those outside everything comes in parables,
L.12: so that seeing they may see and not perceive, and hearing they may hear and not understand, lest they should turn and it be forgiven them."

R.11: Jesus told them, "God has given you the mystery of the kingdom of God. It is a secret that God is now making known to you. But people outside hear everything only in stories.
R.12: So they look and look, but they do not really see. They listen and listen, but they do not understand. Otherwise they might turn back to God and be forgiven."

decisions.choice: mystery: God's secret plan, hidden until God makes it known
decisions.reason: In Daniel 2:28 God "reveals mysteries". The mystery is that God's kingdom is coming in Jesus. It is given, not worked out by cleverness.

decisions.choice: has been given: God has given it
decisions.reason: The passive leaves the giver unnamed; in Jewish speech this often points to God.

decisions.choice: those outside: people who do not come to Jesus to learn
decisions.reason: In 3:31-35 Jesus' own family stand outside, while those who sit around him are his family. Being outside is about response, not birth.

decisions.choice: seeing they may see ... lest they turn: Isaiah 6:9-10
decisions.reason: Jesus uses God's words to Isaiah, who was sent to a people who would not listen. The ending, "be forgiven", matches the ancient Aramaic paraphrase of Isaiah, where the Hebrew has "be healed".

decisions.choice: so that ... lest: Isaiah's words come true in those who refuse to hear
alternatives: so that: only a result, with no purpose
decisions.reason: "So that" usually states a purpose. In Isaiah, God's message hardens those who have already refused it. Some read the clause as a result, or read the last line as a hope that they might yet turn.

decisions.choice: It is a secret that God is now making known to you
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the word "mystery" and adds what it means here.

decisions.choice: look and look, listen and listen
alternatives: seeing they may see, hearing they may hear
decisions.reason: The doubled verbs mean seeing again and again; Balanced and Readable repeat the verb to show this.

decisions.choice: turn back to God
decisions.reason: Readable says who they would turn to.

records.source: Καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Οὐκ οἴδατε τὴν παραβολὴν ταύτην, καὶ πῶς πάσας τὰς παραβολὰς γνώσεσθε;
records.gloss: And he says to them, Not do you know the parable this, and how all the parables will you understand?
pieces: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "Do you not see what this parable means? How then will you understand all the others?

L.13: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says to them, "Do you not understand this parable? And how will you understand all the parables?

R.13: Then Jesus said to them, "You do not understand this story? Then how will you understand any of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} stories?

decisions.choice: says: present tense telling a past event
decisions.reason: As in 4:1, Mark uses the present for vividness.

decisions.choice: this parable is the key to the others
alternatives: Jesus scolds them for being slow
decisions.reason: The parable of the sower is about hearing itself. Whoever misses it will miss the point of the rest.

decisions.choice: do you not understand: may be a question or a statement
alternatives: you do not understand this parable
decisions.reason: Either way, Jesus goes on to explain it.

decisions.choice: my stories
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear the parables are Jesus' own.

records.heading: The seed is the word

records.source: ὁ σπείρων τὸν λόγον σπείρει.
records.gloss: The [one] sowing the word sows.
pieces: The farmer sows the word.

R.14: The farmer plants God's message in people.

decisions.choice: the word: the message of God's kingdom that Jesus preaches
decisions.reason: In Mark "the word" is the good news Jesus speaks (2:2; 4:33).

decisions.choice: the sower: not named
decisions.reason: The explanation is about the seed and the soils. The sower is anyone who spreads the word, first of all Jesus.

decisions.choice: God's message; in people
decisions.reason: Readable says whose word it is and where it is sown, which the next verses show.

records.source: οὗτοι δέ εἰσιν οἱ παρὰ τὴν ὁδὸν ὅπου σπείρεται ὁ λόγος, καὶ ὅταν ἀκούσωσιν εὐθὺς ἔρχεται ὁ Σατανᾶς καὶ αἴρει τὸν λόγον τὸν ἐσπαρμένον εἰς αὐτούς.
records.gloss: These now are the [ones] along the road where is sown the word, and when they hear, immediately comes the Satan and takes away the word having been sown into them.
pieces: Some are like seed sown beside the path. When the word is sown in them and they hear it, Satan comes at once and carries off the word that was planted in them.

L.15: And these are the ones along the path where the word is sown: when they hear, immediately Satan comes and takes away the word that has been sown in them.

R.15: Some people are like the path where the seed fell. They hear God's message, but right away Satan comes. He takes away the message that was planted in them.

decisions.choice: these are the ones along the path: people are pictured as the places where seed falls
decisions.reason: The picture moves between seed and soil. The point is what happens to the word in each kind of hearer.

decisions.choice: Satan: the adversary, the devil
decisions.reason: The birds of 4:4 stand for Satan, who opposes God's work (1:13; 3:23).

decisions.choice: Some people are like
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make the comparison plain.

records.source: καὶ οὗτοί εἰσιν ὁμοίως οἱ ἐπὶ τὰ πετρώδη σπειρόμενοι, οἳ ὅταν ἀκούσωσιν τὸν λόγον εὐθὺς μετὰ χαρᾶς λαμβάνουσιν αὐτόν, καὶ οὐκ ἔχουσιν ῥίζαν ἐν ἑαυτοῖς ἀλλὰ πρόσκαιροί εἰσιν, εἶτα γενομένης θλίψεως ἢ διωγμοῦ διὰ τὸν λόγον εὐθὺς σκανδαλίζονται.
records.gloss: And these are likewise the [ones] upon the rocky [places] being sown, who when they hear the word immediately with joy receive it, \v 17 and not they have root in themselves but temporary are; then having come trouble or persecution because of the word immediately they fall away.
pieces: In the same way, others are like seed sown on rocky ground. When they hear the word, they welcome it at once with joy,
but it takes no root in them, and they last only a short while. Then, when hardship or persecution arises on account of the word, they soon fall away.

L.16: And these likewise are the ones sown on the rocky ground: when they hear the word, they immediately receive it with joy,
L.17: and they have no root in themselves, but they are temporary; then when trouble or persecution comes because of the word, immediately they fall away.

R.16: Other people are like the rocky ground. They hear God's message and right away they accept it with joy.
R.17: But they do not let it go deep into them, so they last only a short time. Then trouble comes, or people treat them badly because of the message. Right away they turn away from it.

decisions.choice: no root in themselves: the word does not go deep into them
decisions.reason: As with the plant in 4:6, there is a quick start but nothing below the surface.

decisions.choice: trouble: pressure, hardship
decisions.reason: The word means pressure from outside, such as suffering for the faith.

decisions.choice: fall away: stumble, give up their trust
decisions.reason: The verb means to be tripped up so as to fall. Jesus uses it of the disciples deserting him (14:27).

decisions.choice: they do not let it go deep into them; they turn away from it
alternatives: they have no root in themselves; they fall away
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture in plain words.

records.source: καὶ ἄλλοι εἰσὶν οἱ εἰς τὰς ἀκάνθας σπειρόμενοι· οὗτοί εἰσιν οἱ τὸν λόγον ἀκούσαντες, καὶ αἱ μέριμναι τοῦ αἰῶνος καὶ ἡ ἀπάτη τοῦ πλούτου καὶ αἱ περὶ τὰ λοιπὰ ἐπιθυμίαι εἰσπορευόμεναι συμπνίγουσιν τὸν λόγον, καὶ ἄκαρπος γίνεται.
records.gloss: And others are the [ones] among the thorns being sown; these are the [ones] the word having heard, \v 19 and the cares of the age and the deceit of the riches and the about the other things desires entering in choke the word, and unfruitful it becomes.
pieces: Still others are like seed sown among thorns. They hear the word,
but worries about this present age, the false promise of wealth, and longing for other things crowd in and smother the word, so that it bears no fruit.

L.18: And others are the ones sown among the thorns; these are the ones who heard the word,
L.19: and the cares of the age and the deceitfulness of riches and the desires for other things come in and choke the word, and it becomes unfruitful.

R.18: Other people are like the ground with thorny weeds. They hear God's message.
R.19: But then they worry about the things of this life. They are fooled by the promise of riches. They want many other things. All these things crowd out the message, so it does not produce anything in their lives.

decisions.choice: cares of the age: worries that belong to life in this present world
decisions.reason: "The age" is the present time, set against the age to come (10:30).

decisions.choice: deceit of riches: wealth promises what it cannot give
decisions.reason: The word means deceit. In some later Greek it means pleasure, and a few read it so here.

decisions.choice: it becomes unfruitful: the word bears no crop in them
decisions.reason: The subject is most likely the word, though the result is the same for the hearer.

decisions.choice: the false promise of wealth
decisions.reason: Balanced says how riches deceive.

decisions.choice: in their lives
decisions.reason: Readable says where the crop should have grown.

records.source: καὶ ἐκεῖνοί εἰσιν οἱ ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν τὴν καλὴν σπαρέντες, οἵτινες ἀκούουσιν τὸν λόγον καὶ παραδέχονται καὶ καρποφοροῦσιν ἓν τριάκοντα καὶ ἓν ἑξήκοντα καὶ ἓν ἑκατόν.
records.gloss: And those are the [ones] upon the soil the good having been sown, who hear the word and receive and bear fruit one thirty and one sixty and one a hundred.
pieces: But others are like seed sown in good soil. These hear the word, welcome it, and bear a crop, thirty, sixty, or a hundred times what was sown."

L.20: And those are the ones sown on the good soil: such as hear the word and accept [it] and bear fruit, thirtyfold and sixtyfold and a hundredfold."

R.20: But some people are like the good soil. They hear God's message and accept it. Then they produce a good crop, thirty, sixty, or even a hundred times as much as was planted."

decisions.choice: receive: accept and hold on to
decisions.reason: The verb is stronger than hearing. It means taking the word in as one's own.

decisions.choice: bear fruit: a life that shows the word at work
decisions.reason: The fruit is what the word produces in the hearer. Mark does not say more.

decisions.choice: one thirty, one sixty, one a hundred: as in 4:8
alternatives: in thirty, in sixty, in a hundred
decisions.reason: The same unaccented letters can be read as "one" or "in". The SBLGNT reads "one". Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: times what was sown (B); times as much as was planted (R)
decisions.reason: As in 4:8.

records.source: Καὶ ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς· Μήτι ἔρχεται ὁ λύχνος ἵνα ὑπὸ τὸν μόδιον τεθῇ ἢ ὑπὸ τὴν κλίνην, οὐχ ἵνα ἐπὶ τὴν λυχνίαν τεθῇ;
records.gloss: And he was saying to them, Not comes the lamp so that under the basket it may be put or under the bed? Not that upon the lampstand it may be put?
pieces: He also said to them, "Is a lamp brought in to be set under a bowl or under a bed? Is it not meant to go on a lampstand?

L.21: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was saying to them, "Does the lamp come in to be put under the basket or under the bed? Is it not to be put on the lampstand?

R.21: Jesus also said to them, "No one brings a lamp into the house and then hides it under a bowl or under a bed. You put it on a stand, where it can give light.

decisions.choice: lamp, basket, bed: a small clay oil lamp, a grain measure, a raised couch
alternatives: a modern lamp, a basket, a bed on the floor
decisions.reason: The basket was a measure for grain, a bowl that could cover a lamp. The bed was a couch raised on legs, used for sleeping or reclining at meals.

decisions.choice: the questions: the first expects "no", the second "yes"
decisions.reason: Nobody hides a lamp; it is brought in to give light.

decisions.choice: comes: the lamp is said to come, not to be brought
alternatives: only a way of saying a lamp is brought in
decisions.reason: The verb is unusual for a lamp. It may hint at Jesus, who came to make things known (1:38).

decisions.choice: two statements in place of questions; where it can give light
decisions.reason: Readable gives the answer the questions expect and says why a lamp goes on a stand.

records.heading: Nothing hidden that will not come to light

records.source: οὐ γάρ ἐστιν κρυπτὸν ἐὰν μὴ ἵνα φανερωθῇ, οὐδὲ ἐγένετο ἀπόκρυφον ἀλλ’ ἵνα ἔλθῃ εἰς φανερόν.
records.gloss: Not for is [anything] hidden except that it be made known, nor has become secret but that it come into the open.
pieces: For nothing is hidden except to be brought out in the open, and nothing has been kept secret except so that it might come to light.

L.22: For there is nothing hidden except to be made known, nor has anything become secret except that it should come into the open.

R.22: Things are hidden only so that later they can be shown. Secrets are kept only so that later they can come out into the open.

decisions.choice: except that it be made known: hiding is for the sake of later showing
alternatives: everything hidden will be found out
decisions.reason: The clauses state purpose. What is now hidden in parables, the mystery of 4:11, is meant to be made plain.

decisions.choice: hidden: God's kingdom is now veiled, but it will be seen
decisions.reason: In this setting the hidden thing is the kingdom, not people's secrets.

decisions.choice: later
decisions.reason: Readable says that the showing comes after the hiding.

records.source: εἴ τις ἔχει ὦτα ἀκούειν ἀκουέτω.
records.gloss: If anyone has ears to hear let him hear.
pieces: If anyone has ears to hear, let that person listen."

L.23: If anyone has ears to hear, let {{gender:them|him}} hear."

R.23: If you have ears, then listen!"

decisions.choice: has ears to hear: is able and willing to take this in
decisions.reason: The same call as in 4:9.

decisions.choice: them (default), him (alternative)
decisions.reason: As in 4:9.

records.source: καὶ ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς· Βλέπετε τί ἀκούετε.
records.gloss: And he was saying to them, Watch what you hear.
pieces: He also said to them, "Pay attention to what you hear.

L.24: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was saying to them, "Take care what you hear.

R.24: He also said, "Think carefully about what you hear.

decisions.choice: watch: take care, pay attention
decisions.reason: The verb means "see", but as a command it means "be careful" (8:15).

decisions.choice: what you hear: the word Jesus speaks
decisions.reason: The command is about attending to the message, which the next saying explains.

records.source: ἐν ᾧ μέτρῳ μετρεῖτε μετρηθήσεται ὑμῖν καὶ προστεθήσεται ὑμῖν.
records.gloss: With what measure you measure it will be measured to you, and will be added to you.
pieces: Whatever measure you use, God will use the same for you, and will give you more besides.

L.24: With the measure you measure [with], it will be measured to you, and more will be added to you.

R.24: As you listen, so God will give to you. In fact, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will give you even more.

decisions.choice: the measure you measure with: you will receive in the way you give
alternatives: a rule about weights in trade
decisions.reason: This is a proverb from buying and selling grain. Here it is about the attention one gives to Jesus' word; it is not a unit of measure.

decisions.choice: it will be measured, it will be added: God will do it
decisions.reason: The passive verbs leave the giver unnamed, pointing to God.

decisions.choice: added: given beyond what is deserved
decisions.reason: God gives more than the measure: those who listen will be given more understanding.

decisions.choice: God
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name God as the one who gives.

decisions.choice: As you listen, so God will give to you
decisions.reason: Readable says what the measure stands for here.

records.source: ὃς γὰρ ἔχει, δοθήσεται αὐτῷ· καὶ ὃς οὐκ ἔχει, καὶ ὃ ἔχει ἀρθήσεται ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ.
records.gloss: Who for has, it will be given to him; and who not has, even what he has will be taken from him.
pieces: Those who have will be given more, and those who do not have will lose even what they have."

L.25: For whoever has, it will be given to {{gender:them|him}}; and whoever does not have, even what {{gender:they have|he has}} will be taken away from {{gender:them|him}}."

R.25: People who have something will be given more. People who have nothing will lose even the little they have."

decisions.choice: has: has received the word and holds it
decisions.reason: In this setting what one "has" is the word that was heard (4:24).

decisions.choice: will be given, will be taken away: God gives and takes
decisions.reason: The passive points to God, as in 4:24.

decisions.choice: those who (B); people who (R)
decisions.reason: Plural forms include men and women without a setting.

decisions.choice: the little
decisions.reason: Readable shows that they had only a little.

records.source: Καὶ ἔλεγεν· Οὕτως ἐστὶν ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ ὡς ἄνθρωπος βάλῃ τὸν σπόρον ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς καὶ καθεύδῃ καὶ ἐγείρηται νύκτα καὶ ἡμέραν, καὶ ὁ σπόρος βλαστᾷ καὶ μηκύνηται ὡς οὐκ οἶδεν αὐτός.
records.gloss: And he was saying, Thus is the kingdom of the God, as a man should throw the seed upon the earth \v 27 and should sleep and rise night and day, and the seed should sprout and lengthen, how not knows he.
pieces: He also said, "It is like this with the kingdom of God: a man throws seed on the ground.
He goes to sleep at night and gets up by day, and the seed sprouts and grows tall, though he does not know how.

L.26: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was saying, "The kingdom of God is like this: as if a man should throw seed on the ground
L.27: and sleep and rise night and day, and the seed sprouts and grows, he does not know how.

R.26: Jesus also said, "This is what the kingdom of God is like. Think of a man who plants seed in the ground.
R.27: Each night he goes to sleep, and each day he gets up. All the while, the seed comes up and grows. He does not know how it happens.

decisions.choice: the seed grows without the man's help or knowledge
decisions.reason: The point is that God makes the kingdom grow. The man's part is to sow and later to reap.

decisions.choice: night and day: day after day
decisions.reason: Jews counted the day from evening, so night comes first.

decisions.choice: grows: lengthens, grows tall
decisions.reason: The verb means to become long, as a stalk does.

decisions.choice: Each night he goes to sleep, and each day he gets up
alternatives: sleep and rise night and day
decisions.reason: Readable pairs each action with its time.

records.heading: Seed that grows by itself

records.source: αὐτομάτη ἡ γῆ καρποφορεῖ, πρῶτον χόρτον, εἶτα στάχυν, εἶτα πλήρης σῖτον ἐν τῷ στάχυϊ.
records.gloss: Of itself the earth bears fruit, first blade, then ear, then full grain in the ear.
pieces: The earth bears its crop on its own: first the green blade, then the ear, then the ear full of grain.

L.28: By itself the earth bears fruit, first a blade, then an ear, then full grain in the ear.

R.28: The ground makes the plants grow all by itself. First a green shoot comes up. Then the head of grain forms. Then the head fills up with grain.

decisions.choice: of itself: without human work
decisions.reason: The word means "automatic". The growth comes from what God has made, not from the farmer.

decisions.choice: blade, ear, full grain: the stages of wheat or barley
decisions.reason: First the green shoot, then the ear or head, then the ripe grain filling the head.

decisions.choice: full grain: the SBLGNT has the form of "full" that does not change its ending
alternatives: a form of "full" that agrees with "grain"
decisions.reason: Manuscripts differ in the form of the word, not in the sense. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: head of grain
decisions.reason: Readable uses the plainer word for an ear of grain.

records.source: ὅταν δὲ παραδοῖ ὁ καρπός, εὐθὺς ἀποστέλλει τὸ δρέπανον, ὅτι παρέστηκεν ὁ θερισμός.
records.gloss: When but permits the fruit, immediately he sends the sickle, because has come the harvest.
pieces: And when the grain is ready, he puts in the sickle at once, because harvest time has come."

L.29: But when the fruit allows, immediately he sends in the sickle, because the harvest has come."

R.29: When the grain is ripe, the man goes right away and cuts it, because it is time to gather the harvest."

decisions.choice: permits: when the crop is ready
decisions.reason: The fruit "allows" the harvest when it is ripe.

decisions.choice: he sends the sickle, the harvest has come: Joel 3:13
decisions.reason: Joel pictures God's judgment as a harvest: "Put in the sickle, for the harvest is ripe." The harvest is the end, when God gathers in his kingdom.

decisions.choice: the man goes and cuts it
decisions.reason: Readable says what sending the sickle means.

records.source: Καὶ ἔλεγεν· Πῶς ὁμοιώσωμεν τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ, ἢ ἐν τίνι αὐτὴν παραβολῇ θῶμεν;
records.gloss: And he was saying, How shall we compare the kingdom of the God, or in what it parable shall we put?
pieces: He also said, "What shall we liken the kingdom of God to? What parable shall we set beside it?

L.30: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was saying, "How shall we compare the kingdom of God, or by what parable shall we present it?

R.30: Jesus also said, "What is the kingdom of God like? What story can we use to picture it?

decisions.choice: shall we: Jesus draws the hearers into the search
decisions.reason: A teacher's way of asking the listeners to think with him.

decisions.choice: put: set out, present
decisions.reason: The verb means to set a picture before the hearers.

records.heading: The smallest of seeds

records.source: ὡς κόκκῳ σινάπεως, ὃς ὅταν σπαρῇ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς, μικρότερον ὂν πάντων τῶν σπερμάτων τῶν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς καὶ ὅταν σπαρῇ, ἀναβαίνει καὶ γίνεται μεῖζον πάντων τῶν λαχάνων καὶ ποιεῖ κλάδους μεγάλους, ὥστε δύνασθαι ὑπὸ τὴν σκιὰν αὐτοῦ τὰ πετεινὰ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ κατασκηνοῦν.
records.gloss: As a grain of mustard, which when it is sown upon the earth, smaller being of all the seeds that [are] upon the earth, \v 32 and when it is sown, it grows up and becomes greater than all the garden plants and makes branches great, so that able to be under the shade of it the birds of the sky to nest.
pieces: It is like a mustard seed. When it is sown in the ground, it is smaller than every other seed on earth.
But once it is sown, it shoots up and becomes bigger than all the garden plants. It sends out branches so large that the birds of the sky can settle in its shade."

L.31: [It is] like a grain of mustard, which, when it is sown on the ground, is smaller than all the seeds that are on the earth,
L.32: and when it is sown, it grows up and becomes greater than all the garden plants and makes great branches, so that the birds of the sky are able to nest under its shade."

R.31: It is like a mustard seed. It is the smallest seed a farmer plants.
R.32: But after it is planted, it grows bigger than all the other plants in the garden. Its branches grow so big that birds can come and make their nests in its shade."

decisions.choice: smaller than all the seeds: the smallest seed people knew to sow
alternatives: the smallest seed in the whole world
decisions.reason: The mustard seed was proverbially tiny (Matthew 17:20). Jesus speaks of what his hearers sowed, not of all plants.

decisions.choice: mustard: a garden plant that grows taller than a man in a season
decisions.reason: Black mustard grew in Galilee and could reach several feet high, large enough for birds to sit in.

decisions.choice: birds nesting in its shade: a great kingdom that shelters many
decisions.reason: The prophets use this picture of a great kingdom (Ezekiel 17:23; 31:6; Daniel 4:12). Some see the nations coming in; Mark does not say.

decisions.choice: the sky: the air above the earth
decisions.reason: The word means heaven or sky; birds of the sky are wild birds.

decisions.choice: split into several sentences
decisions.reason: The Greek sentence repeats "when it is sown" and runs on. Balanced and Readable break it up.

decisions.choice: make their nests
decisions.reason: The verb means to settle or live in a shelter. Readable uses the simplest picture.

records.source: Καὶ τοιαύταις παραβολαῖς πολλαῖς ἐλάλει αὐτοῖς τὸν λόγον, καθὼς ἠδύναντο ἀκούειν·
records.gloss: And with such parables many he was speaking to them the word, as they were able to hear;
pieces: With many parables like these {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} spoke the word to them, as much as they were able to hear.

L.33: And with many such parables {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was speaking the word to them, as they were able to hear;

R.33: Jesus used many stories like these to teach people God's message. He taught them as much as they could understand.

decisions.choice: as they were able to hear: as much as they could take in
alternatives: in a way that hid the meaning from them
decisions.reason: Jesus fitted his teaching to his hearers. The verse balances 4:11-12.

decisions.choice: the word: the message of God's kingdom
decisions.reason: As in 4:14.

decisions.choice: God's message
decisions.reason: As in 4:14.

records.source: χωρὶς δὲ παραβολῆς οὐκ ἐλάλει αὐτοῖς, κατ’ ἰδίαν δὲ τοῖς ἰδίοις μαθηταῖς ἐπέλυεν πάντα.
records.gloss: without but parable not he was speaking to them, privately but to the own disciples he was explaining all things.
pieces: He would say nothing to them without a parable, but in private {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made everything plain to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own disciples.

L.34: and without a parable {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did not speak to them, but privately {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} explained everything to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own disciples.

R.34: He always used stories when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} taught the crowds. But when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was alone with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} told them what everything meant.

decisions.choice: explained: untied, solved
decisions.reason: The verb means to loosen or solve, as one solves a riddle.

decisions.choice: was speaking, was explaining: this was his habit
decisions.reason: The verbs describe what he did again and again.

decisions.choice: the crowds
decisions.reason: Readable names who "them" are.

records.source: Καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ὀψίας γενομένης· Διέλθωμεν εἰς τὸ πέραν.
records.gloss: And he says to them on that the day, evening having come, Let us go across to the other side.
pieces: As evening came on that day, Jesus said to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples, "Let us go across to the far side of the lake."

L.35: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says to them on that day, when evening had come, "Let us go across to the other side."

R.35: That evening Jesus said to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers, "Let us go across to the other side of the lake."

decisions.choice: says: present tense telling a past event
decisions.reason: As in 4:1.

decisions.choice: the other side: the eastern shore of the lake
decisions.reason: The east side was largely Gentile country; they land in the region of the Gerasenes (5:1).

decisions.choice: his disciples/followers; of the lake
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say who "them" are and what they are crossing.

records.heading: Even the wind and the sea obey {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}

records.source: καὶ ἀφέντες τὸν ὄχλον παραλαμβάνουσιν αὐτὸν ὡς ἦν ἐν τῷ πλοίῳ, καὶ ἄλλα πλοῖα ἦν μετ’ αὐτοῦ.
records.gloss: And having left the crowd, they take along him as he was in the boat, and other boats were with him.
pieces: They sent the crowd away and took {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} along in the boat, since {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was already in it. Other boats also went with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

L.36: And leaving the crowd, they take {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} along, just as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was, in the boat; and other boats were with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

R.36: The followers left the crowd. Jesus was already in the boat, so they took {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with them. Some other boats went along too.

decisions.choice: as he was in the boat: he was already in the boat from 4:1
decisions.reason: They set off without going ashore first.

decisions.choice: take along: present tense telling a past event
decisions.reason: As in 4:1.

decisions.choice: other boats: others came with them
decisions.reason: Mark mentions them but says nothing more of them.

decisions.choice: since he was already in it (B); was already in the boat (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable follow the meaning note.

records.source: καὶ γίνεται λαῖλαψ μεγάλη ἀνέμου, καὶ τὰ κύματα ἐπέβαλλεν εἰς τὸ πλοῖον, ὥστε ἤδη γεμίζεσθαι τὸ πλοῖον.
records.gloss: And comes a storm great of wind, and the waves were throwing into the boat, so that already was being filled the boat.
pieces: A fierce windstorm blew up, and the waves were crashing into the boat, so that it was already filling with water.

L.37: And a great windstorm comes up, and the waves were breaking into the boat, so that the boat was already filling.

R.37: Then a very strong wind began to blow. Big waves crashed into the boat. Soon the boat was starting to fill with water.

decisions.choice: a great windstorm: a sudden squall on the lake
decisions.reason: The lake lies low among hills, and winds can sweep down on it without warning.

decisions.choice: comes: present tense telling a past event
decisions.reason: As in 4:1.

decisions.choice: already filling: the boat was in real danger
decisions.reason: The water was coming in faster than they could deal with.

decisions.choice: with water
decisions.reason: English needs to say what filled the boat.

records.source: καὶ αὐτὸς ἦν ἐν τῇ πρύμνῃ ἐπὶ τὸ προσκεφάλαιον καθεύδων· καὶ ἐγείρουσιν αὐτὸν καὶ λέγουσιν αὐτῷ· Διδάσκαλε, οὐ μέλει σοι ὅτι ἀπολλύμεθα;
records.gloss: And he was in the stern on the cushion sleeping. And they wake him and say to him, Teacher, not is it a concern to you that we are perishing?
pieces: Jesus {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} was asleep on the cushion at the back of the boat. They woke {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and said, "Teacher, does it mean nothing to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} that we are going to die?"

L.38: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} was in the stern, sleeping on the cushion. And they wake {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and say to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Teacher, is it not a concern to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} that we are perishing?"

R.38: Jesus was at the back of the boat, sleeping with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} head on a cushion. The followers woke {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} up. They said, "Teacher, do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} not care that we are going to die?"

decisions.choice: he himself: Jesus set against the frightened disciples
decisions.reason: The pronoun is stressed. While they struggle, he sleeps.

decisions.choice: the stern, the cushion: the raised back of the boat and the cushion kept there
decisions.reason: The article points to the boat's own cushion, perhaps one used by the helmsman or a sandbag for ballast.

decisions.choice: we are perishing: we are about to die
decisions.reason: The verb means to be destroyed. They fear drowning.

decisions.choice: is it not a concern to you: a question of reproach
decisions.reason: The disciples ask as if he did not care. The form expects the answer "yes, I care".

decisions.choice: at the back of the boat
decisions.reason: "Stern" is a sailor's word. Balanced and Readable describe the place.

decisions.choice: with his head on
decisions.reason: Readable pictures how the cushion was used.

records.source: καὶ διεγερθεὶς ἐπετίμησεν τῷ ἀνέμῳ καὶ εἶπεν τῇ θαλάσσῃ· Σιώπα, πεφίμωσο.
records.gloss: And having been woken he rebuked the wind and said to the sea, Be silent, be muzzled.
pieces: Jesus woke, rebuked the wind, and commanded the sea, "Silence! Be still!"

L.39: And being woken, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} rebuked the wind and said to the sea, "Be silent! Be muzzled!"

R.39: Jesus woke up and gave the wind a strong command. Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to the lake, "Be quiet! Be still!"

decisions.choice: rebuked: gave a stern command
decisions.reason: The same verb is used when Jesus silences unclean spirits (1:25; 3:12).

decisions.choice: be muzzled: the word Jesus spoke to the unclean spirit (1:25)
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks to the storm as to a hostile power. The form means "be still and stay so".

decisions.choice: Jesus commands wind and sea
alternatives: a lucky change in the weather
decisions.reason: In the Scriptures God stills the storm (Psalm 107:29) and sets limits to the sea (Job 38:8-11).

decisions.choice: Silence! Be still! (B); Be quiet! Be still! (R)
decisions.reason: "Muzzled" in English suggests an animal. Balanced and Readable give the sense; Literal keeps the picture.

decisions.choice: gave the wind a strong command
decisions.reason: Readable says what "rebuke" means here.

records.source: καὶ ἐκόπασεν ὁ ἄνεμος, καὶ ἐγένετο γαλήνη μεγάλη.
records.gloss: And ceased the wind, and there was a calm great.
pieces: The wind dropped, and a great calm came over the water.

L.39: And the wind ceased, and there was a great calm.

R.39: The wind stopped blowing, and the water became very calm.

decisions.choice: a great calm: set against the great storm (4:37) and the great fear (4:41)
decisions.reason: Mark repeats "great" to show the change. The calm is as complete as the storm was fierce.

decisions.choice: came over the water
decisions.reason: Balanced says where the calm was.

records.source: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Τί δειλοί ἐστε;
records.gloss: And he said to them, Why fearful are you?
pieces: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} asked them, "Why are you so afraid?

L.40: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "Why are you fearful?

R.40: Jesus said to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers, "Why are you so afraid?

decisions.choice: fearful: timid, lacking courage
decisions.reason: The word means cowardly or timid, not reverent awe.

decisions.choice: why are you fearful: the SBLGNT has no "so"
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add "so". Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: so
decisions.reason: "So" gives the tone of the question in natural English; it does not follow the added word in some manuscripts.

records.source: οὔπω ἔχετε πίστιν;
records.gloss: Not yet do you have faith?
pieces: Is there still no faith in you?"

L.40: Do you not yet have faith?"

R.40: Do you still not have faith in {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}?"

decisions.choice: not yet: the SBLGNT reads "not yet"
alternatives: how is it that you have no faith
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts read "How is it that you have no faith?" The earliest read "Do you not yet have faith?" Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: faith: trust in Jesus and in God's power at work in him
decisions.reason: After all they have seen, they still do not trust him in danger.

decisions.choice: in me
decisions.reason: Readable says whom they should trust.

records.source: καὶ ἐφοβήθησαν φόβον μέγαν, καὶ ἔλεγον πρὸς ἀλλήλους· Τίς ἄρα οὗτός ἐστιν ὅτι καὶ ὁ ἄνεμος καὶ ἡ θάλασσα ὑπακούει αὐτῷ;
records.gloss: And they feared a fear great and were saying to one another, Who then this is, that even the wind and the sea obey him?
pieces: Great fear came over them, and they kept saying to one another, "Who is this, then, that wind and sea alike obey {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}?"

L.41: And they feared a great fear and were saying to one another, "Who then is this, that even the wind and the sea obey {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}?"

R.41: The followers were now terrified. They asked each other, "Who is this man? Even the wind and the water obey {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}!"

decisions.choice: they feared a great fear: the awe of people before God's power
decisions.reason: The same words describe the sailors in Jonah 1:16 after God calmed the sea. Now they fear the one in the boat more than the storm.

decisions.choice: who then is this: only God rules wind and sea
decisions.reason: The question is left for the reader to answer from the Scriptures (Psalm 107:29) and from Mark's first line (1:1).

decisions.choice: were saying: they kept asking
decisions.reason: The verb describes ongoing talk.

decisions.choice: were now terrified
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the strength of the fear with a plain word.
